_about: Manifest for tools/fetch_sources.py and tools/build_kb.py. fetch_sources.py materializes each entry's `fetch` block as the PDF named in `pdf` (under knowledge-base/pdfs/, not committed); build_kb.py cuts that PDF into chunks. Each entry names a source, how its sections are headed, and how to link to a section. Entries are listed in precedence order: statute and CFR, the ACS, FAA guidance, then rulemaking preambles.

_notes: The ecfr.gov section links are the canonical citation for a CFR section and do not depend on the PDF. The CFR PDFs are printed from the eCFR renderer at fetch time, so they carry the current text; the annual edition on govinfo.gov is two-column and lags.
The AC, study-guide, ACS, sample-question, and handbook links point at the PDF and a page; confirm the URLs against faa.gov when you fetch, since FAA moves files.

heading presets: cfr matches '§ 107.41 Title.'; numbered matches '5.2 Title' at the top level; chapter matches 'Chapter 3' headings. A custom regex with a (?P<section>...) group, and optionally a (?P<title>...) group, is accepted in place of a preset. The whole line is consumed by the heading, so a title group should run to the end of the line when body text follows the heading on the same line (AC 107-2A).

A heading that repeats within a source (a running header, a task letter reused across ACS areas) gets a numbered file name instead of overwriting the earlier chunk; the builder reports how many, so a regex that matches running headers is visible.
layout: false reads a PDF in reading order instead of physical layout. Use it for two-column documents (the handbook chapters, the U.S. Code); layout mode interleaves their columns.
The FAA web pages change without notice; the fetch log records when each was read. The Federal Register preambles are chunked by Federal Register page so that each chunk cites as 86 FR <page>.
